data.name: Dierdre
data.gender_notes: Dierdre is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Irish 'Déirdre' meaning 'little dark one' or 'sorrowful one'. In Irish mythology, Dierdre was a beautiful and tragic heroine who caused the great love of Fionn mac Cumhail for her, leading to the tragic Fionnghuil cycle. The name Dierdre carries the meaning “Little Dark One” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Dierdre usually hope their child will grow to embody little dark one and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes deep emotions and the power of love.
data.etymology: Dierdre belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Little Dark One.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dierdre total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Dierdre has a deep cultural history in Ireland. In the Irish mythological tales, Dierdre was represented as a cursed and beautiful woman who seduced the greatest hero Fionn mac Cumhail, leading to tragic consequences. Her story is told in the ancient folklore consisting of the Fionnghuil cycle. Dierdre's name is still resonant in Irish culture and history, connecting people with their mythology and past.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Dierdre holds spiritual significance for its symbolism of love, passion, and sorrow. In Irish mythology, it represents the complexities of human emotions and desires. The name can be seen as a reminder of the powerful yet destructive nature of love and how it can lead to both joy and sorrow. It's a name that evokes passion and reminds us to be aware of the potential consequences of our desires.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Dierdre: Irish derived from the Old Celtic word "deir" meaning "fear" or "terror." In Christian tradition, it symbolizes courage in the face of fear or adversity. It is a name for those who, despite their fear, choose to press on with faith and determination.

biblical_reference.note: The name Dierdre does not have a direct reference in the Bible.

historical_references.reference: Dierdre is a legendary Irish heroine, the daughter of the high king of Ireland, Conchobar mac Nessa.
historical_references.context: Dierdre is a central character in the Irish mythological cycle, the Táin Bó Cúailnge.
